The Cedars School
The Cedars School Vision
At The Cedars, our vision is to create a school where every child feels emotionally safe, valued and ready to learn.
We believe that children need to feel emotionally safe, develop trusting relationships and experience a strong sense of belonging before they are able to fully access learning. We therefore place equal importance on pupils' academic, social and emotional development.
Our approach is relational, compassionate and ambitious. We recognise that every child is unique, with their own strengths, interests, experiences and starting points. We work to understand and remove barriers to learning so that every child can make progress, develop confidence and experience success.
Our school values provide a shared framework for how we learn, work and treat one another:
Through these values, we aim to develop pupils' self-worth, resilience, communication, cooperation, problem-solving and independence, preparing them to thrive both in school and beyond.
We believe that every child should have access to a broad, balanced and ambitious curriculum. Lessons and activities are carefully planned and adapted to meet individual needs, enabling pupils to achieve their personal goals and make progress from their individual starting points.
We work in partnership with parents and carers, staff, governors and external professionals to provide the best possible educational experience for every pupil and to prepare our children and young people to become confident, responsible and active members of their communities.

Curriculum Intent
The Cedars curriculum is broad, balanced, ambitious and inclusive. It prioritises the key knowledge, skills, vocabulary and understanding that we believe our pupils need to develop as they progress through the school and prepare for their next steps.
Our curriculum recognises that pupils join The Cedars with different experiences, strengths, needs and starting points. Learning is therefore carefully sequenced and adapted so that pupils can access ambitious content at an appropriate level of challenge.
We do not reduce our ambitions for pupils because they have additional needs. Instead, we identify and remove barriers to learning and provide the adaptations, support and opportunities pupils need to participate, succeed and make progress.

About Us
School Opening Hours 8.45-3.15pm Monday-Thursday and 8.45-1.30pm Fridays.
Children attend school for 30.75 hours in a typical week.
Our pupils travel from a range of locations - Transitions can be difficult for our children, particularly at the beginning and end of the school day. To support this we have a 'soft start and finish' to each day. Pupils can arrive between 8.45-9am and they leave between 3-3.15pm (Mon-Thurs) and at 1.30pm on Fridays.
Children travelling with parents/carers should enter through the main school entrance. Children arriving by minibus will enter the school through the rear doors.
Telephone: 0208 230 0015
Email: office@cedars.hounslow.sch.uk
Lisa Welch (Deputy Head) is the SEND lead.
Please contact the school office if you would like a paper copy of any of the documents contained within this website.

Welcome to The Cedars School
The Cedars School is a special school for children who have an EHCP (Education, Health and Care Plan) with a primary need of SEMH (Social, Emotional and Mental Health) difficulties. For a large number of our pupils, these difficulties co-occur with other areas of need, including autism, speech, language and communication needs and ADHD.
The school is located in extensive, wooded grounds in Cranford, which lies in the London Borough of Hounslow.
Children are taught in classes with a teacher and at least one teaching assistant. The school recruits, trains and deploys staff to best meet the needs of our pupils. Staff are supported by therapists who are part of the school staff team.
Children are taught through an adapted curriculum based on the National Curriculum, which is differentiated to meet the wide range of abilities and needs of the children who attend the school. Children are also encouraged to take part in a wide range of visits, sporting events, clubs and opportunities that build upon and support both academic and social skills.
Whilst many of our children are not drawn from the immediate local community, the school has excellent links with parents and carers, with many opportunities provided to attend the school for performances, open days and other events. The school plays a full and active part in our local community and has close links with local organisations, businesses and community groups. Our Governing Body plays an active role in school life and supports the school's links with the wider community.
If you feel that your child would benefit from attending the school, you should contact the London Borough of Hounslow's Special Educational Needs team in the first instance.

The Cedars School is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children. All staff and volunteers are expected to share this commitment.

Safeguarding at The Cedars School is everyone’s responsibility all of the time. All staff and visitors are expected to:
If you are ever concerned about the safety or well‐being of someone at our school please talk to the school’s Designated Safeguarding Leads (DSL):
DSL/ Prevent Leads: Tessa Reed (Headteacher) and Lisa Welch (Deputy Headteacher)
In the event the DSL being absent, the following members of staff have been trained as Deputy Designated Safeguarding Leads:
Designated Safeguarding Deputies: Ben Smith, Katie Deadman-Salter, Mary Farmer and Joanna Williams.

SEND Information
All pupils currently attending The Cedars School have an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP) or are in the process of statutory assessment. Social, Emotional and Mental Health (SEMH) is the primary area of need for pupils attending The Cedars, and many pupils also have identified needs in one or more of the other broad areas of SEND.
Pupils may have additional needs relating to communication and interaction, cognition and learning, sensory and/or physical needs. Some pupils also have diagnosed or emerging neurodevelopmental needs, including autism and ADHD.
At The Cedars, we recognise that every pupil has a unique profile of strengths, needs, experiences and starting points. Our provision is therefore personalised to individual pupils and informed by their EHCP, assessment information, professional advice and ongoing observation.
It is our intention to provide every child with the best possible education within a safe, supportive and stimulating environment. We strive to promote self-worth, confidence and respect so that every pupil can make progress and achieve their potential.
Central to our approach is equality of opportunity throughout the school. All pupils are supported to participate fully in the life and curriculum of the school, and reasonable adjustments are made where required to remove barriers to participation.
Through the commitment and dedication of our staff, working in partnership with pupils, parents and carers, professionals and governors, we aim to provide an education of the highest quality that enables every pupil to thrive.

Remote Education Provision
The Cedars School uses Google Classroom to support remote education when pupils are unable to attend school. Every pupil has their own Google Classroom login and pupils are familiar with using the platform as part of their learning in school.
Where remote education is required, work will be set by the class teacher or a member of the Senior Leadership Team. This will be appropriate to the pupil's age, developmental level and individual needs. Where appropriate, teachers will provide feedback on work through Google Classroom. During any extended periods of absence please contact the school if you do not have technology and we will arrange for a Chromebook to be sent home.
For longer periods of absence, or where a pupil is unable to access online learning, the school will provide additional or alternative resources to support learning at home. These may include printed worksheets and practical activities to develop key skills such as handwriting, fine motor skills, reading, mathematics, communication and independence.
As all pupils at The Cedars School have special educational needs, remote education is planned and adapted with pupils' individual needs in mind. Where appropriate, parents and carers will be supported with resources and guidance to help their child engage with learning at home.
Parents and carers can contact the school for support with remote education through their child's class email address, the school email address (help@cedars.hounslow.sch.uk), or by contacting the school office.

Parent/Carers
The Cedars School values the support and engagement of all parents and carers. Whilst we may not be close to every child’s home, we make every effort to stay in regular communication and invite parents and carers in to the school whenever possible.
Staff communicate daily via email and regularly follow up these emails with phone calls home. We host three parents evenings a year but parents are always welcome to book an appointment to meet with school staff to discuss specific issues.
We host regular opportunities for parents and carers to visit the school in a less formal setting through art days, school performances and sports days.
If you do have any general queries about the school please email office@cedars.hounslow.sch.uk and a member of staff will deal with your request.

Family Group
At The Cedars School we host a weekly Family Group.
Family Group helps children who are struggling at school and supports them to reach their full potential.
In Family Group, parents/carers come into school each week to work together with their children. In the group children and parents/carers talk, play, listen, have fun, and work on change. Families help families, sharing ideas, sorting problems and learning from each other.
Families can come to the group for as long as they want and they find that week by week, little by little, small steps lead to big changes.
​Family Group was set up by The School and Family Works; a team of experienced, fully qualified, practical therapists passionate about helping children and their families.

Parent Pay
ParentPay - our online payment service
We are pleased to announce that we accept payments online for dinner money and school uniform.
Using a secure website called ParentPay you can pay online using your credit/debit card or continue to make cash payments at PayPoint stores. ParentPay will be our preferred method of making payments to school.
What are the benefits to parents & pupils?
What are the benefits to our school?
We will send you your account activation details. Once you receive these:
If you have any questions, please contact the school finance office. For more information, visit www.parentpay.com/parents/.
Improves school security
ParentPay FAQs
Once you have received your activation letter from school with your activation login details you will be able to activate your account and start making payments. This letter will be sent to you soon by your school.
ParentPay accepts MasterCard, Visa and American Express credit cards, and Maestro, Switch, Delta, Electron, Solo and Visa debit cards. Some schools may limit the use of credit cards for some transactions; you will be informed by the school directly of any such restrictions.
Yes. ParentPay uses leading technology to process your card transactions securely. All communication with the bank is encrypted and neither ParentPay nor the school have access to your card details.
Standard website addresses begin with http: the address for a secure site will always begin with https. You will also see a padlock at the bottom/top right of the screen on our login page and after you have logged into your account; never enter your card details or personal data on any web page whose address does not start https.
ParentPay Limited, and its group companies, operate in full compliance with Data Protection Law; Including the Data Protection Act 1998 and the General Data Protection Regulation (EU) 2016/679.
The ParentPay Terms and Conditions include a Data Processing Agreement (DPA), compliant with the GDPR, which details both parties’ obligations relating to Data Protection. https://www.parentpay.com/schools/school-terms-and-conditions/
The ParentPay Privacy Notice, which is available to end-users, provides further information on the processing activities undertaken by ParentPay. https://www.parentpay.com/privacy-policy/
ParentPay will NEVER contact you by phone, email or mail and ask you to divulge confidential information like passwords or card numbers.
If you are ever contacted by someone claiming to be from ParentPay, please contact us immediately on 02476 994 820.
Why not visit your local library, internet café or see if you can get access to a computer at work. Alternatively, ask if you can use your school’s computers. Many schools have computers available for parents and will be happy to show you how to use them.
For more information please visit www.parentpay.com
